AMZN’s 2024-Q1 print shows a clear profitability and cash-flow inflection alongside re-accelerating higher-margin growth engines. Revenue grew 13% YoY (ex-FX) to $143.3B, but the more tradeable signal is operating leverage: operating income surged to $15.3B (+221% YoY) and trailing 12-month adjusted FCF swung to $48.8B (+$53.2B YoY). Historically, this extends a multi-quarter margin expansion and supports the view that prior cost resets are now flowing through sustainably rather than as a one-quarter anomaly.

Versus peers in the provided snapshot, AMZN screens as an outperformer on quantified profit/FCF momentum (peer-relative +0.62), while still matching the sector’s AI narrative. Importantly, AWS growth re-accelerated to 17.2% from 13.2% in Q4, and advertising grew 24%—two signals that demand and monetization are improving in segments that typically carry better incremental margins. The “multibillion-dollar” GenAI run-rate adds upside optionality, but is less actionable than the AWS/ads growth rates.

Key bullish drivers: continued AWS re-acceleration, sustained ad growth, and further margin/FCF compounding if fulfillment speed improvements translate into retention and basket expansion. Key bearish/downside drivers: macro sensitivity (rates ~5.33% and yields ~4.16% can pressure valuation multiples), FX and geopolitical volatility, and any demand softness that would quickly reduce operating leverage given AMZN’s fixed-cost base. Net: constructive but not one-way—momentum is strong, while macro/FX and cyclicality keep risk elevated.

AMZN’s 2024-Q2 print shows a clear quality upgrade: revenue grew a solid +11% YoY (ex-FX) while operating income surged +91% and trailing 12-month adjusted FCF inflected to $51.4B (+$44.7B YoY). Historically, the Q1 revenue pause followed by a Q2 step-up supports re-acceleration, and the margin/FCF trajectory suggests durable operating leverage rather than a one-off. AWS is the key swing factor for multiple expansion; growth accelerated to 18.8% from 17.2% QoQ, aligning with broader enterprise AI demand seen across peers. Ads (> $50B TTM; +$2B YoY) adds a higher-margin, more resilient profit stream that can offset retail cyclicality.

Versus peers, AMZN is not the fastest top-line grower (MSFT’s select software assets are growing faster), but it is outperforming on profitability momentum and cash generation at scale—supporting a modest positive peer-relative stance. The most tradable signals here are (1) AWS re-acceleration, (2) sustained margin/FCF expansion, and (3) ads monetization scale.

Upside drivers: continued AWS/AI demand translating into higher cloud margins; further retail fulfillment efficiency; ads mix shift; internal AI productivity (Amazon Q) compounding cost leverage. Downside drivers: high-rate macro (5.33% policy rate) pressuring valuation and consumer demand; AWS growth re-deceleration amid competition; reinvestment/CapEx re-acceleration that could cap FCF; leap-day benefit modestly flattering NA growth. Net: constructive but not euphoric—execution is strong, but macro/valuation sensitivity keeps risk elevated.
